message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine appropriate crime(s) based on facts. The facts: Defendant set fire to property (corn husk, corn cobs, then house interior) causing damage valued 17905 yuan. This is arson (放火) or intentional arson. In examples, similar facts: using lighter to set fire to house, they labeled as 放火. Example: Wu case (set fire to house) => 放火. Also example: Li case (set fire to hotel items) => 故意毁坏财物 (but that was multiple breakings, not fire). For fire, they used 放火. Also "失火" used when fire caused unintentionally (e.g., accidental). Here it's intentional to vent emotions, so it's arson. So answer: [罪名]放火<eoa>. Possibly also "故意毁坏财物" but fire is arson. In Chinese criminal law, arson is "放火罪". So final answer.
